core.title: Set feature size to max(DESIRED OUTCOME size, Footprint size) and split features over limits
core.given: Any feature plan (new or existing, with or without complete size, covers_desired_outcomes and footprint fields)
core.when: The planner creates, edits (including prose-only) or validates that feature plan
core.then: Ensure the feature's size field is present and equals exactly max(DESIRED OUTCOME size, Footprint size), with the DESIRED OUTCOME bracket from covers_desired_outcomes and the Footprint size from the footprint point score.
prefer: Derive the DESIRED OUTCOME size bracket from covers_desired_outcomes and score the footprint with the point system (defined in the companion convention planner.feature.size-max-rule); take the larger.

Split a feature whose footprint exceeds component/event limits; always split one exceeding hard limits (tables/jobs/integrations); limit values come from the companion convention planner.feature.hard-limits.
If covers_desired_outcomes or footprint is missing, fill it in from the feature's scope before setting size; do not guess a size without both inputs.
avoid: A size differing from max(DESIRED OUTCOME size, Footprint size), e.g. using only one of the two.
Leaving an over-limit feature unsplit, even when only editing its prose.
Trimming covers_desired_outcomes or under-reporting footprint to lower size or dodge a limit.
core.why: The convention defines feature size as the larger of the DESIRED OUTCOME bracket and the footprint's architectural-complexity score, and requires features over component/event or hard limits to be split.
evidence: Validator recomputes DESIRED OUTCOME size from covers_desired_outcomes and Footprint size from footprint points and checks size == max of the two; a missing size field is a failure.
Where covers_desired_outcomes or footprint is missing, the validator reports the size as unverifiable (not as passing).
Validator checks footprint counts against component/event limits and hard limits (tables/jobs/integrations); any excess without a split is a failure.
verification: A sizing validator recomputes the DESIRED OUTCOME size bracket from covers_desired_outcomes and the Footprint size from footprint points, and compares the declared size field against the max of the two; a missing size field is a failure.
Where covers_desired_outcomes or footprint is missing, the size is reported as unverifiable, not as passing.
Footprint counts are checked against component/event limits and hard limits (tables/jobs/integrations); any excess without a split is a failure.
The check runs over all feature plans (existing and new), not only changed sizing fields.

The numeric point system and limit values are not defined by this rule: the check requires them from the companion conventions that define the max rule (planner.feature.size-max-rule) and the limit values (planner.feature.hard-limits).
Detecting absent or changed sizing fields needs a field-level observer over feature plan documents; the validator computes the bracket and score itself rather than trusting the declared size.
Term gloss (validation_rule): a feature sizing/limit validation rule; this rule is exactly that, and its verifier scope is feature sizing and limit checking.

values: size field set, changed or missing
size != max(DESIRED OUTCOME size, Footprint size)
size unverifiable because covers_desired_outcomes or footprint is missing

fires: Planner authors a new feature plan, with or without sizing fields filled in yet.
Planner adds or removes DESIRED OUTCOMES in covers_desired_outcomes of an existing feature.
Planner adds components, events, tables, jobs or integrations to a feature's footprint.
Planner makes a prose-only edit to a feature whose existing size is wrong or whose footprint already exceeds a limit.
Planner validates/reviews existing feature plans, including ones missing size, covers_desired_outcomes or footprint.
A feature's footprint exceeds the component/event limits or the hard limits for tables/jobs/integrations.
doesNotFire: Editing a product capability, DESIRED OUTCOME or acceptance document when no feature plan's sizing inputs or validity are affected.
Implementation work in application layers that does not touch plan artifacts.

neutralityNotes: This convention is planner-methodology-level and was already essentially stack-neutral: feature plan, DESIRED OUTCOME, covers_desired_outcomes, footprint and their sizing terms name plan-artifact concepts (DESIRED OUTCOME and feature are plan artifacts of the ATDD method), so the agent-facing texts are kept verbatim. The only stack-dependent input is how a feature plan document is concretely identified, which the profile supplies via roles.plan_artifact.kinds and roles.assignment (the Bun sidecar says: by artifact kind/location in the planning tree). Companion convention references (planner.feature.size-max-rule, planner.feature.hard-limits, and the noted split suggestion planner.feature.split-on-limits) are corpus-level rule ids, retained by name for faithfulness; another stack realization maps them to its own ids for the same companion conventions. The term gloss 'validation_rule: a feature sizing/limit validation rule' is general planning terminology and is carried in the core's verification array, not as a Bun-only item; nothing in bun.json remains Bun-specific, so bunOnly is empty. Per the sidecar's own split suggestion, `then` carries only the size obligation; the split obligation remains in prefer[1]/avoid[1] with its enforcement in the verification array, so the core is no stronger and no weaker than bun.json.
